records.title: Narrative entry

fields.event: Went to battle stations and commenced attack at 0030. at 0045 SJ made initial contact at 10000 yards, target on port bow, course north, speed 10.5. This is the first time our radar has picked up a target and functioned properly during the current war. When range had been decreased it was seen that other two ships were escort vessels small DD's, corvettes or mine layers. We decided to concentrate torpedoes on big ship since it must be especially valuable with two escorts. No other ships seen or contacted in SJ sweep.

records.source: Part VII summary of submarine attacks
records.title: Attack 1 · Pass. Freighter

fields.narrative: at 0104 fired four torpedoes, ten second interval, no spread, straight bow shot, 80° starboard track and then swung right to clear formation. First hit looked to be a magnetic explosion, ship seemed to jump out of water and streak of flame twice ships length on water line. Second hit under bridge, large column of water and smoke. Third hit heard and felt throughout ship but not observed; we were concentrating on getting clear at that time fourth, missed. One escort vessel went down torpedo track and not finding us they opened with searchlight. Just at this time an explosion occurred on the target, evidently gasoline as a bright flame shot up 200 feet in air and completely enveloped the ship. Also lit us up like a church. We could even see the camouflage on the escorts.

records.title: Attack 2 · DM or Small DD

fields.narrative: One escort at least opened fire at us and picked us up in the searchlight, range closing rapidly even at our best speed. about a half dozen shells hit around us; ducked at range of 1700 yards at 0118 and fired one stern tube at the trailing escort as we went down. This probably saved our necks as later events indicated that he had to maneuver to avoid and thus lost a golden opportunity. We probably made the all time record from surface to 100 feet but the planes jammed and we set another record for coming up to 35 feet. Finally got control in hand power and went down again.

records.title: Depth charging by escorts

fields.event: As we passed 140 feet one escort came overhead and let go a close barrage. This kicked out main motor overload relays but we regained power immediately. Also opened valve on fresh water system and angle on the boat caused about 1000 gallons of fresh water in #1 FWT to run aft into #3 FWT, thereby messing up the trim since this was not discovered until surfacing. The after bridge loud speaker diaphragm was ruptured as was also discovered on surfacing. The usual cork, paint, gauge glasses, meters, depth gauges and loose gear were knocked about but no serious damage. He then let go another barrage ahead of us. Not so close. Two more came ten minutes later further away. The escorts then pulled out of sound range so we surfaced at 0235 about 8000 yards from the burning target.
fields.damage: kicked out main motor overload relays; opened valve on fresh water system causing about 1000 gallons of fresh water in #1 FWT to run aft into #3 FWT; after bridge loud speaker diaphragm ruptured; cork, paint, gauge glasses, meters, depth gauges and loose gear knocked about

records.title: Rendezvous with USS Guardfish

fields.event: 0510 sighted submarine bearing 346°T. exchanged recognition signals with U.S.S. GUARDFISH. She advised that she was in contact with convoy 15 miles astern on base course 150°T, speed 9. We got on convoy's track and opened out to southward from GUARDFISH who submerged about 0800. In order to increase range of visibility and be in position to communicate by radio we stayed on surface speed 5 knots, on convoy's track until 1300.
